messages:
Sam: FYI seeing intermittent allreduce stalls on g5x nodes in us-west-2 for ~2h. p99 token latency jumps from ~40ms -> 300-800ms, NCCL retries and hangs. mlx5 rx counters ticking up :thinking:
Priya: which nodes and can you paste NIC counters?
Sam: affected: gw-g5x-03, gw-g5x-07, gw-g5x-11. Quick dump:
```
# on gw-g5x-03
cat /sys/class/net/ens5/statistics/rx_errors
186
mlxrxtool query port0 | grep -i rx
rx_crc_errors: 24
rx_discard: 92
rx_missed: 18
```
John: rx_discard + rx_crc usually means MTU/frame mismatch or offload inconsistency. Any recent firmware/kernel pushes?
Maya: we rolled mlx5 fw 1.3.2 -> 1.3.4 last night. us-west was staged yesterday morning. gw-g5x-07 was in that batch.
Priya: fwdiff shows `mcg_mode` default flipped on some hosts. ip link shows mtu 9000 on some hosts and 9216 on others (weird).
Sam: NCCL/GPUDirect assumes consistent MTU; odd MTU mix could fragment. But why CRCs instead of just drops?
John: CRCs when link-level frames truncated/fragmented. If a switch or host doesn't accept larger frames or offload combos (VXLAN + NIC offloads) are mismatched, you get crc + discard.
Maya: repro steps: run `nccl-tests all_reduce` across 4 GPUs and watch ibverbs logs. ~70% runs show stalled allreduce that recovers after retries.
Sam: logs show repeated -127 returns from ibverbs and `RNR_RETRY_EXC_ERR` in dmesg -> mlx5.
Priya: checklist to validate: `ip link show ens5`, `ethtool -k ens5`, `rdma-linklatency` or `rdma_pingpong` between peers, check rp_filter sysctl and any eBPF/NAT rewriting.
John: rp_filter=1 + asymmetric path is a classic RoCE killer. Also verify `tx-checksumming` and GRO/GSO state.
Sam: ran checks: two hosts had mtu 9216, others 9000. ethtool shows tx-checksumming: on everywhere. rp_filter=1 on gw-g5x-07.
Maya: temporary reproduce: set rp_filter=0 and align MTU to 9000 on the 9216 hosts and rerun nccl tests.
infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-0427 (P2): "intermittent NCCL allreduce stalls - us-west-2 g5x pool" assigned eng-runtime/infra.
Priya: vendor notes: fw 1.3.4 has a known regression when `mcg_mode` enabled + MTU > 9000, can cause tx scheduling/backpressure. Opening VID-8792 with diagnostics attached (dmesg, mlxrxtool).
John: propose remediation plan:
1) Align MTU to 9000 cluster-wide as a temporary mitigation.
2) Set net.ipv4.conf.all/rp_filter=0 on affected hosts while we triage.
3) Canary rollback of mlx5 fw to 1.3.2 on a single host and stress test (NCCL+iperf).
4) If canary good, roll back batch or push vendor driver fix.
Sam: executed MTU align + rp_filter=0 on gw-g5x-07. After change, test job p99 dropped to ~55ms and crc counters stable for 15m.
Maya: running `rdma_pingpong` and `iperf3 --udp -b 40G` between gw-g5x-03 and gw-g5x-11 to confirm link-level loss.
Sam: iperf3 UDP 40G bursts showed ~2.6% loss for 30s bursts; kernel dmesg had `tx_dma_busy` warnings.
Priya: that matches fw release notes. Recommend canary rollback. Also add short-term alert for rx_crc>10 over 5m per-node.
John: I'll coordinate rollback window with netops/colocation. Also check `mlx5_esw_get_port_counters` for `rx_no_buf` / `rx_mbuf_alloc_failed`. If those rise, driver memory tunables might be needed.
Maya: I'll collect NCCL debug traces (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO/DEBUG) and nvprof traces on canary runs and post them here.
Sam: positive outcome on canary rollback needed to validate. If rollback fails, vendor patch path only.
Priya: vendor ticket VID-8792 updated with sample traces and packet captures.
John: long-term actions:
- Add preflight for fw+driver compatibility matrix in rollout playbooks.
- Prevent MTU drift via autoscaler scripts (lock MTU on provisioning).
- Add monitoring for rx_crc/rx_discard > threshold per GPU pool.
Maya: adding temporary eng-runtime alert for rx_crc>10 over 5m/node.
Sam: thanks all. I'll keep thread updated during canary window.
Priya: assigned to @John for rollback coordination.
John: will schedule canary in next 2 hours and report back here. :thumbsup:
